description: Three boxes connected by rightward arrows show the flow from receiving input through temporary computation to producing output. The left box, “Input space,” lists input data. The middle box, “Temporary space,” lists temporary data, stack frames, and instructions, in that order. The right box, “Output space,” lists output data.

frames.explanation: The brace labeled “Space usually counted in space complexity” spans temporary and output space only, excluding input space. The chapter's convention also typically ignores instruction space within temporary space. The main items counted are therefore temporary data, stack frames, and output data.
frames.title: What space do we usually count?

summary: The figure divides the space an algorithm uses into three categories. A brace marks those usually counted.
title: What space do we usually count?
